title: Hospital Quality Management
shortDescription: How hospitals actually measure and improve quality — KPIs, clinical audits, mortality review, and the problem-to-improvement cycle underneath all of it.
genZNote: A hospital can't improve what it doesn't measure — this is the measuring part.

sections.heading: Quality Indicators and KPIs
bullets: Quality indicator — a measurable element of care used to assess quality (e.g. surgical site infection rate).
KPI (Key Performance Indicator) — a quality indicator specifically chosen as a priority target for an organisation, often tied to a numeric goal.
Clinical audit — a systematic review of clinical practice against defined criteria, to identify gaps in care delivery.
Infection indicators, medication errors, and patient safety events — commonly tracked, high-priority indicator categories.
Mortality review — structured review of deaths to identify preventable factors and system learnings.
Patient satisfaction and patient experience — tracked alongside clinical indicators, not instead of them.

sections.heading: From Problem to Improvement
sections.body: Hospital quality management follows a consistent analytical path from a raw problem to an actual system-level fix — this is the same underlying logic as root cause analysis, generalised beyond individual incidents to ongoing performance data.

steps.name: Problem
steps.explanation: A quality gap is identified — through data, a complaint, or an audit finding.
steps.purpose: The starting trigger for the entire improvement cycle.

steps.name: Data
steps.explanation: Relevant data is gathered — indicator trends, audit results, incident reports.
steps.purpose: Improvement decisions must be evidence-based, not assumption-based.

steps.name: Analysis
steps.explanation: The data is analysed to understand the pattern, scale, and contributing factors.
steps.purpose: Separates a one-off blip from a genuine systemic issue.

steps.name: Root cause
steps.explanation: The underlying, system-level cause is identified — not just the immediate trigger.
steps.purpose: Fixing symptoms without the root cause guarantees recurrence.

steps.name: Corrective action
steps.explanation: A specific action is implemented to address the root cause.
steps.purpose: Turns analysis into an actual operational change.

steps.name: Monitoring
steps.explanation: The indicator is tracked after the change, to see if it actually moved.
steps.purpose: Confirms the fix worked — don't assume, verify.

steps.name: Improvement
steps.explanation: Sustained, monitored gains are locked into the new standard of practice.
steps.purpose: Completes the loop — this becomes the new baseline, not a one-time win.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Hospital quality management runs on measurable indicators (KPIs, clinical audits, mortality review, patient experience) fed through a Problem → Data → Analysis → Root cause → Corrective action → Monitoring → Improvement cycle.
keyFacts: A KPI is a quality indicator specifically prioritised as an organisational target.
Clinical audit compares actual practice against defined criteria — it's a comparison exercise, not just data collection.
Mortality review looks specifically for PREVENTABLE factors, not just cause of death.
The improvement cycle always ends in monitoring — a fix isn't complete until its effect is verified.
commonConfusion: Every KPI is a quality indicator, but not every quality indicator is a KPI — a KPI is specifically one an organisation has prioritised and set a target for.

highYieldFacts: The Problem → Data → Analysis → Root cause → Corrective action → Monitoring → Improvement sequence is the core hospital quality-improvement logic.
Mortality review specifically targets preventability, not just cause-of-death recording.
commonTraps: Treating 'quality indicator' and 'KPI' as identical terms — KPI is the prioritised subset.
mustRemember: Every improvement claim needs a monitoring step afterward — without it, you don't actually know if the fix worked.

confusedTerms.distinction: A quality indicator is any measurable element of care quality. A KPI is a quality indicator an organisation has specifically prioritised as a target, usually with a numeric goal attached.
